title: France enters technical recession after third-quarter GDP contracts by 0.2%
seoTitle: France enters technical recession with Q3 GDP contraction
dek: France has entered a technical recession after the national statistics agency INSEE revised third-quarter GDP downward to a 0.2% contraction.
happened: On 27 November 2026, France's National Institute of Statistics (INSEE) published final data showing that the French economy contracted by 0.2% in the third quarter of 2026, according to reports from informat.ro and ara.cat. This revision worsened an initial estimate of a 0.1% decline. INSEE also adjusted second-quarter data to a slight contraction, marking two consecutive quarters of economic decline and triggering a technical recession. According to ideal-investisseur.fr and startupfortune.com, exports dropped by 1.6% while business investment fell by 0.9% during the summer months. Household consumption rose slightly by 0.3%, but foreign trade subtracted 0.6 percentage points from gross domestic product. The economic slowdown complicates minority government budget negotiations and deficit reduction goals. Meanwhile, the Bank of France anticipates moderate growth in the final quarter of the year, with official data scheduled for release on 29 January 2027.

sides.says: INSEE reported that the French economy contracted by 0.2% between July and September, following a revised contraction in the previous quarter, meeting the criteria for a technical recession.
Finance Minister Roland Lescure called for swift approval of the 2027 budget and stated that the 5% deficit target is non-negotiable despite economic headwinds.
Governor Emmanuel Moulin stated that "We don't see a recession coming, we see positive growth in Q4," expecting moderate economic expansion in the final quarter.

next: INSEE is scheduled to publish its first estimate for fourth-quarter economic growth on 29 January 2027.
summary: France entered a technical recession after official figures showed back-to-back quarters of economic contraction. INSEE revised third-quarter GDP down to a 0.2% decline, driven by falling exports and weaker business investment. The downturn complicates government efforts to pass the 2027 budget and curb public debt, while financial institutions project potential moderate growth in the fourth quarter.
